name: booba project
iocPatterns: Ransomware executables with varied naming conventions
Scripts for automated reconnaissance prior to infection
Usage of multi-stage downloaders for initial payloads
Communication with C2 infrastructure via standard web ports
recommendedActions: Implement Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all external business systems.
Maintain offline, immutable backups of critical organizational data and configuration files.
Deploy Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions to monitor for unauthorized script execution.
Restrict administrative privileges to only essential staff members on a least-privilege basis.
Segment internal networks to isolate high-value production systems from public-facing endpoints.
Conduct routine security awareness training focusing on identifying spear-phishing attempts.
Block known malicious file types and scripts (e.g., .js, .vbs, .ps1) at the email gateway.
Apply latest security patches to all internet-reachable software and firmware.
campaignsText: The Booba project shows a consistent pattern of targeting diverse commercial enterprises across international boundaries. Their campaign history—linking to various instances such as 'Upstaging', 'Frosty Acres Brands', and targeting specific companies like Jani-King and Telewave, Inc.—indicates an active operational cycle focused on high-impact ransomware delivery_The inclusion of varied industrial targets suggests they may leverage automated discovery or broad phishing campaigns to identify viable victims for extortion.
description: Booba project is a criminal threat actor primarily engaged in ransomware and extortion operations to achieve financial gain. The group targets a broad range of sectors, including technology, manufacturing, and architectural services, demonstrating activities across multiple notable organizations.
goals: The primary strategic objective for Booba project is direct financial gain through ransomware and potential data leakage extortion. They do not appear to have a specific geopolitical agenda; instead, they target organizations based on the perceived value of the victim's assets and their ability to pay significant ransoms. Their targets include manufacturing firms (e.g., Oklahoma Manufacturing Alliance), technology providers (e.g., Zynex, Telewave, Inc.), and professional service firms (e.g., Pelli Clarke Pelli Architects), suggesting a 'wide-net' approach to identifying victims with high impact potential.
